name: Asphalt
desc: A road plane running out to the horizon under standing water — stone aggregate set in bitumen, two tyre tracks polished darker than the lane between them, a crack net opening through the patches, dashed markings streaming toward the viewer, and the lamps down the road smeared into long streaks on the wet film.

sheen.doc: water on the road: 0 = bone dry and matte · 1 = a standing film that mirrors the lamps into long streaks

scale.doc: how wide the road reads — lane width, aggregate size and marking scale together

energy.doc: how hard the reflected lamps burn on the wet film

density.doc: aggregate coarseness, crack density and how much of the road is patched

hue.doc: tints the bitumen and the lamps (34 = true warm-lamp-on-cold-tar)

speed.doc: how fast the road runs toward the viewer

x.doc: vanishing point across the frame — swings the road left or right

y.doc: horizon height — how much of the frame the plane takes

style.doc: wet: rain-slick tarmac, the lamps down the road drawn out into long streaks · dry: matte and chalky, the aggregate reading hard and bright · worn: patched and cracked, markings faded back to nothing · sodium: a monochrome sodium-vapour night, amber on near-black · contour: non-representational — a pavement survey, the surface as pure elevation contour lines, no material at all

act.doc: drift: the road runs past at a walk · haul: a night drive, markings streaming · stall: nearly stopped, the wet film and the lamps doing all the work

seed.doc: a different stretch of road — new aggregate, cracks, patches and lamp positions
